from_trouble: none — this is not a defect report. It came from Akien ruling on an open spec question the preceding voyage deliberately left with him (`does the trail stay append-only at all, or does a validation collapse to one current record per proof?`), captured verbatim at CairnCommons/ideas/2026-08-16-does-the-trail-stay-append-only-at.json.
intention: A validation trail collapses to ONE current record per proof, and a verdict CHANGE stops being an unread entry and becomes an event fired out a door at the moment it happens.
why:
AKIEN'S OWN WORDS, and the design follows them rather than paraphrasing them: "the validation is a single record. so is the preceeding one. so a ticket should accumulate them? and all we need to keep of a proof is enough data to verify it. So do we need it's whole history? no, in fact it tends to create noise." (2026-08-16, captured verbatim at CairnCommons/ideas/2026-08-16-does-the-trail-stay-append-only-at.json.)

THE LIVED SYMPTOM, stated as an end-user experience rather than a virtue: a mind opens a validation trail to find out whether a proof passes, and reads sixteen dated records to learn one fact. Fifteen of them describe a world that no longer exists, and a model reader weights whatever sits in context as present tense — so the noise is not merely wasted bytes, it is stale claims read as current.

AND IT IS MEASURED, not asserted. 90 trails, 283 entries, 470KB. Every reader in the corpus takes the newest record and only the newest — orient.py:206 (`latest = recs[-1]`), quorum.py:147, validation_store.standing() — with zero reads of any other index anywhere in cairn/, skills/, bin/, CairnCommons/ or ~/.cairn. So 193 entries, 68% of the store and ~320KB, are read by nothing. THE SECOND MEASUREMENT IS THE ONE THAT TURNED A DISK ARGUMENT INTO A DESIGN ONE: of 54 multi-entry trails, 52 never change verdict, and the two that do carry the SAME red — `bwrap: Can't chdir to <stale path>` — both stamped 2026-07-24T15:35:49. One environment fault, recorded twice, is the entire information content of 193 historical entries.

WHERE THE LINE FALLS, and it did not need inventing: `source_fingerprint` (validation_store.py:143) is already one sha256 over every .py in the component root, already rides in the record's evidence, and is already compared against the working tree by standing(). Akien's "enough data to verify it" is exactly that, which is what makes ONE record sufficient rather than merely smaller — a record whose fingerprint still matches the tree speaks about the world as it is; one whose fingerprint has moved is expired, and its predecessors are more expired still.

THE COST IS THE MECHANISM, NOT THE BYTES. The hash chain exists solely to police entries nobody reads: every write recomputes a digest over the whole trail, inspect_trail runs three eligibility-nested lanes over it, standing() is built on it, and the immediately preceding voyage was spent narrowing that gate. The chain never bought unforgeability — anyone can recompute it — it bought append-only-ness, which is the property being deliberately dropped. What keeps the door's one-path claim standing without it: the 0444 mode bit, the corpus scan for second writers, and git, which holds the pre-change bytes of all 90 trails and was the stronger instrument in the preceding voyage.

TRACES TO CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-an-artifact-is-present-tense-or-past-tense-never-both.md — ruled 2026-08-15, and it carries this decision in almost Akien's words ('history creates noise'; a present-tense artifact is rewritten whole; 'git keeps every prior version, so the rewrite loses nothing'). The validation trail is absent from that piece's past-tense list (history, slates, voyages, decisions, ideas) while being read by default at every gate — so it is a present-tense artifact that has been accumulating past tense, and this is that piece applied to it. Under it, Law 1: 68% of the store's entries are read by nothing and every reader still opens the whole file.

constraint_commit_before_collapse: A BUILD CONSTRAINT, NOT HYGIENE. The archive claim behind this whole design is 'git keeps every prior version, so the rewrite loses nothing' — measured true (90 of 90 trails git-tracked) but CONDITIONAL: git holds only what was committed. A collapse landing on an uncommitted trail loses the prior record irretrievably. The build commits the standing trails before it collapses them, and falsifier clause (2) is that condition made falsifiable.
distinctions_recorded: ACCUMULATE WHERE A NAMED READER ASKS A CROSS-RUN QUESTION, AND THE READER MUST EXIST. This reconciles the node with ticket the-proof-record-persists-so-runs-can-be-compared, which wants accumulation and is not in conflict: it has a named reader ('which checks have never redded') and is building the store for it; the validation trail has none, measured at zero. The rule outlives this node.

LAW 7 IS SURVIVED BY THE SECOND HALF, NOT WAVED PAST. persist_validation's docstring calls the trail a record of truth under Law 7, and Law 7's why is that an error must not be smoothed into a coherent shape. The test is whether the collapse makes an error QUIETER: today a red sits at index 1 of a 16-entry file nothing reads; under this design a verdict change fires out a door at the moment it happens, into a store that really is append-only. Louder, not quieter — but only with the change-door, which is why falsifier clause (1) is exactly that and why this cast spawns no children.

A CHECK THAT GOES RED AT THE MOMENT ITS CONDITION IS SATISFIED, third instance. Retiring the chain would leave the_door_is_the_only_path_in_practice counting TRAIL_LINK absence in a world where nothing writes TRAIL_LINK — firing forever on a finding false by construction. Caught at the cast rather than in flight; its retirement is bound into this voyage.

CC'S NEAR-MISS, RECORDED BECAUSE THE REASONING IS THE REUSABLE PART: a digest-only spine was nearly designed, keeping each superseded record's 64-byte trail_link so the chain would still verify. That is preserving a mechanism after its job has ended, dressed as thrift. The chain's job was append-only-ness, and append-only-ness is the thing being dropped.
